race_context: Anderson Community Schools serves most of the city of Anderson in Madison County plus Country Club Heights, Edgewood, River Forest, Woodlawn Heights and most of Chesterfield {wiki_acs}; the district lists 12 schools and centers, including one high school, Anderson High School {acs_home}{acs_ref}. A current enrollment figure was not found in fetched sources.
Joe Cronk has been superintendent since March 2020 (interim, then permanent from 2021) and plans to retire effective June 30, 2027 {hb_supt_search}.

The board has seven members elected to four-year terms in even-year November elections from South, East and Central districts and at large {acs_board}. Current members are Mandy Webb (president, South), Patrick Hill (vice president, East), Holly Renz (East), Rodney Chamberlain (at large), Martha Green (South), Robert Bookhart (Central) and JoAnna Collette (at large) {acs_board}{hb_webb_pres}.

Four seats are on the 2026 ballot, matching the state list's four vote-for-1 contests: incumbents JoAnna Collette (at large), Robert Bookhart (Central) and Patrick Hill (East) are running, while Mandy Webb did not file for her South District seat, leaving it open {hb_15filed}{acs_board}.

2026 is the first Indiana election in which school board candidates could declare a party affiliation; in Anderson, two candidates filed as Democrats, one as a Republican and one as an Independent {hb_9filed}{hb_partylabels}.

Budget and referendum: on June 8, 2026 the board voted unanimously to ask voters Nov. 3 to renew the 2018 operating referendum at up to $0.1077 per $100 of assessed value for 2027-2034, raising about $2.9 million a year {hb_ref_june}{acs_ref}. The district attributes its shortfall to state property tax caps, inflation and state funding levels and says the renewal alone will not close it {acs_ref}; at a Sept. 24, 2026 meeting officials put the deficit at $5.5 million without the referendum and $2.6 million with it {hb_ref_sept25}.

Superintendent contract and search: in September 2025 the board voted 4-3 to extend Cronk's contract through 2026-27 after public comment from supporters and critics, including criticism of test scores {hb_cronk_ext}; in September 2026 the board reported 699 survey responses and five town halls and said the job posting had closed Sept. 8 {hb_supt_search}.
Test scores: ACS's IREAD-3 pass rate fell 3.5% in 2026 results while the statewide pass rate was 88.7%, according to the Herald Bulletin {hb_iread}.
Meeting access: after complaints about a 4 p.m. special meeting on June 22, 2026, the board adopted an interim policy in July 2026 holding meetings at 6 p.m. unless there is an emergency {hb_june22}.

The board's leadership vote in January 2026 split 4-3 (Webb, Hill, Green and Renz for Webb; Bookhart, Collette and Chamberlain for Collette), the same alignment as the 2025 contract-extension vote {hb_webb_pres}{hb_cronk_ext}.

Forums: no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire was found in fetched sources. A Herald Bulletin columnist reported in September 2026 that several candidates have the support of board member Holly Renz and that social media posts have urged defeat of the referendum {hb_negative}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent at-large board member seeking a second term; listed on the state ballot list as Nonpartisan {hb_15filed}{in_list}.
background: Holds the at-large seat whose term ends in December 2026 {acs_board}.
Gave the board's June 8, 2026 presentation on the district's finances and the proposed operating referendum renewal {hb_ref_june}.
path_to_ballot: Was among the first candidates to file in May 2026 and did not declare a party {hb_filingstarts}{hb_15filed}.

items: In her June 2026 presentation she said the district faces a $6.1 million annual deficit and projected losses of at least $23.8 million over eight years, including at least $11 million from state property tax reductions and at least $12.8 million from required charter school revenue sharing {hb_ref_june}.

Said of the referendum: “The referendum is not a magic fix. It’s not a blank check, and it’s not a way to avoid hard decisions. It’s one part of a responsible plan to keep current local support in place, while this district also has to make reductions.” {hb_ref_june}

In July 2026 she said a June 22 special meeting was needed to fill principal vacancies so appointees could prepare for the school year; the board then unanimously adopted an interim policy holding meetings at 6 p.m. unless there is an emergency {hb_june22}.

on_incumbent: In August 2025 she moved to postpone a vote on Superintendent Joe Cronk's contract, citing the need for more time to consider public comments {hb_cronk_retire}.
Voted against the one-year extension of Cronk's contract, which passed 4-3 in September 2025 {hb_cronk_ext}.
Received three votes for board president in January 2026; the board elected Mandy Webb 4-3 {hb_webb_pres}.

candidates.summary: Challenger to incumbent Patrick Hill in the East District; ran for the board in 2024; listed on the state ballot list as Nonpartisan {in_list}{hb_15filed}{hb_2024_priorities}.
background: In 2022 he co-led a citizens committee urging ACS to apply for a federal Next Generation School Improvement Grant; the Herald Bulletin then described him as a frequent critic of the district {hb_2022_committee}{hb_2022_grants}.
Ran unsuccessfully for the East District seat held by Holly Renz in 2024 {hb_2024_priorities}{hb_webb_pres}.
Said in 2024, “I’m a product of ACS.” {hb_2024_change}
path_to_ballot: Filed by the June 18, 2026 deadline without declaring a party {hb_15filed}.

items: In his 2024 campaign he expressed concern about ACS ILEARN scores, saying, “If you do not accept your failure, how do you know how to fix it?” and that he wanted teachers “given the tools to be successful” {hb_2024_priorities}.
In 2024 he said ACS had lost 1,000 students since 2018 and that the district should report why families leave and adjust to retain them {hb_2024_change}.
In June 2022 he emailed the board and superintendent proposing a meeting of administrators, board members, union representatives and educators to plan for the next round of grants {hb_2022_grants}.

on_incumbent: In 2024 he said change starts with the school board, which must ensure everyone is treated fairly and equally {hb_2024_change}.
